season.evidence: Logged ascents by this route name fall in Jan, Mar, Apr, May, Jun (5 of 9 in May). Web search found no dedicated season page for the couloir; related Olympic guidance favours snow-covered gullies before July because the rock loosens as it melts out, matching the stored Apr-Jun window.

track.why: Logged route is "Honeymoon colouir" (a synonym of the couloir), 9 May 2026, successful summit, round trip from the Upper Dungeness trailhead (start/end within 41/24 m of our pin, summit 54 m from our pin); report describes the ~50 degree snow couloir with axes and crampons. The 7 May 2026 track (3187657, "NE Couloir/Honeymoon Route") is an equally valid alternative; this one chosen for its description.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Also qualifies (named NE Couloir/Honeymoon Route, 7 May 2026, complete); not chosen only because it has no description text.
24 May 2025 report says it followed the standard route on snow, logged as Deception-Martin Saddle.
August, no route named; the report describes the standard scramble gullies.
Logged as Royal Basin (standard line), August.

facts.text: In early May the couloir snow turns soft and sloppy by late morning, so plan to be back down it before the sun has worked on it.
In early May other parties often climb and descend the couloir at the same time; wait for them to clear rather than climbing beneath them.
In early May water runs freely beside the trail up to roughly 5,700 ft, so there is no need to melt snow on the way in.

notes: Standard Scramble (Royal Basin) is stored separately and already has tracks. Several summer tracks with no route name (e.g. 2932432, 2975164, 3036679) fit the standard scramble, not this couloir.
